Timeline::year¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::year() const

Aliases: y(), yr(), years(), and year_().

Read The Civil Year¶

year() replaces every timestamp with the four-digit year shown by the timeline’s current timezone. It is an elementwise projection: rank, shape, and element order are unchanged, while the result dtype is int32.

The word civil matters near a New Year boundary. year() answers which year the local date belongs to. It does not return the ISO week-numbering year; a date such as 1 January 2021 can therefore have year() == 2021 and week() == 53 at the same time.

Missing timestamps become -1. Treat that value as a missing-field sentinel, not as a historical year. Use isvalid() when the distinction matters.

Example: Years, Boundaries, And Missing Values¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.year());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[2020, 2021, 2024, -1]

The first two values deliberately straddle midnight. The extraction is elementwise, so neither ordering nor adjacency changes the answer.

Timezone Changes The Calendar View¶

The stored instant and its displayed calendar year are different concepts. tz_convert() preserves the instant but changes the local calendar used by all field extractors. Near midnight, converting timezones can therefore change the year. Convert first, extract second when grouping by a local reporting calendar.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • year() does not mutate the timeline and does not return timestamps.

  • A result of -1 means the source element was NaT; it is not a valid year.

  • Do not combine year() and week() as an ISO year-week key at New Year.

  • The aliases are exact synonyms; they do not use different calendars.

See Also¶

  • month: extract the month within the civil year.

  • week: extract the ISO week number.

  • is_leap_year: classify each local calendar year.
